# SQL Query to Retrieve Budget by Department

Here are several SQL query options to retrieve budget information by department, depending on your database structure:

## Basic Query (Assuming a simple department_budget table)
```sql
SELECT
    department_id,
    department_name,
    budget_amount
FROM
    department_budgets
ORDER BY
    department_name;
```

## Query with Department and Budget Details (More comprehensive)
```sql
SELECT
    d.department_id,
    d.department_name,
    d.location,
    b.budget_year,
    b.budget_amount,
    b.allocated_amount,
    b.spent_amount,
    (b.budget_amount - b.spent_amount) AS remaining_budget
FROM
    departments d
JOIN
    budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
WHERE
    b.budget_year = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE) -- or specify a year
ORDER BY
    d.department_name;
```

## Query with Department Hierarchy
```sql
SELECT
    d.department_id,
    d.department_name,
    p.department_name AS parent_department,
    b.budget_amount,
    b.budget_year
FROM
    departments d
LEFT JOIN
    departments p ON d.parent_department_id = p.department_id
JOIN
    budgets b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
WHERE
    b.budget_year = 2023 -- specify year
ORDER BY
    p.department_name, d.department_name;
```

## Query with Budget Breakdown by Category
```sql
SELECT
    d.department_name,
    bc.category_name,
    SUM(b.amount) AS category_budget
FROM
    departments d
JOIN
    budget_items b ON d.department_id = b.department_id
JOIN
    budget_categories bc ON b.category_id = bc.category_id
WHERE
    b.budget_year = 2023 -- specify year
GROUP BY
    d.department_name, bc.category_name
ORDER BY
    d.department_name, category_budget DESC;
```

## Query with Year-over-Year Comparison
```sql
SELECT
    d.department_name,
    b1.budget_year AS current_year,
    b1.budget_amount AS current_budget,
    b2.budget_year AS previous_year,
    b2.budget_amount AS previous_budget,
    (b1.budget_amount - b2.budget_amount) AS budget_change,
    ROUND(((b1.budget_amount - b2.budget_amount) / b2.budget_amount) * 100, 2) AS percent_change
FROM
    departments d
JOIN
    budgets b1 ON d.department_id = b1.department_id AND b1.budget_year = 2023
JOIN
    budgets b2 ON d.department_id = b2.department_id AND b2.budget_year = 2022
ORDER BY
    d.department_name;
```

Note: You'll need to adjust table and column names to match your actual database schema. Common table names might include:
- `departments` or `department`
- `budgets` or `department_budgets`
- `budget_items` or `budget_details`
